item.text:
<thoughtml version="1.0">
  <context>
    <decision id="single_award_funding">Select one proposal for funding under a one-award budget constraint.</decision>
    <criterion_set>
      <criterion>scientific_or_technical_impact</criterion>
      <criterion>strength_of_preliminary_evidence</criterion>
      <criterion>clarity_of_milestones</criterion>
      <criterion>delivery_capability</criterion>
      <criterion>execution_risk</criterion>
      <criterion>value_for_money</criterion>
    </criterion_set>
  </context>

  <options>
    <option id="proposal_a" label="Technically ambitious proposal">
      <summary>High-upside project with substantial novelty and strong preliminary evidence.</summary>
      <strengths>
        <item>Potential for outsized scientific and practical impact.</item>
        <item>Preliminary data reduces concern that the core idea is purely speculative.</item>
        <item>Could establish leadership in an emerging area if successful.</item>
      </strengths>
      <risks>
        <item>Execution path is less predictable.</item>
        <item>Milestones are less clearly defined and may be harder to monitor.</item>
        <item>Delivery team appears less proven for complex program execution.</item>
      </risks>
    </option>

    <option id="proposal_b" label="Safer proposal">
      <summary>Lower-risk project with clear milestones, stronger delivery confidence, and a more experienced team.</summary>
      <strengths>
        <item>Implementation plan is concrete and auditable.</item>
        <item>Experienced team improves confidence in on-time delivery.</item>
        <item>Milestones support active portfolio management and accountability.</item>
      </strengths>
      <risks>
        <item>Expected impact may be more incremental.</item>
        <item>Lower novelty may reduce strategic upside.</item>
        <item>May miss an opportunity to back a potentially field-shifting idea.</item>
      </risks>
    </option>
  </options>

  <evidence>
    <item source="proposal_a" type="preliminary_evidence" weight="high">
      Strong early results support technical plausibility of the ambitious approach.
    </item>
    <item source="proposal_a" type="innovation_potential" weight="high">
      The proposal could generate disproportionate returns if the approach scales.
    </item>
    <item source="proposal_b" type="milestone_quality" weight="high">
      Milestones are specific, sequenced, and suitable for progress tracking.
    </item>
    <item source="proposal_b" type="team_experience" weight="high">
      The delivery team has a stronger record of executing comparable projects.
    </item>
    <item source="both" type="budget_constraint" weight="high">
      Only one award can be made, so portfolio diversification is not available as a risk-management strategy.
    </item>
  </evidence>

  <panel_positions>
    <position member="innovation_focused_reviewers" stance="favor_proposal_a">
      The combination of high ambition and credible preliminary evidence justifies taking risk for potentially transformative impact.
    </position>
    <position member="delivery_focused_reviewers" stance="favor_proposal_b">
      With only one award available, the panel should prioritize execution confidence, milestone clarity, and team capability.
    </position>
    <position member="chair" stance="leans_proposal_b">
      Proposal A is scientifically compelling, but the single-award constraint increases the cost of execution failure.
    </position>
  </panel_positions>

  <tradeoff>
    <tension>transformative_upside_vs_delivery_certainty</tension>
    <interpretation>
      The choice is not between strong and weak science, but between higher upside with greater execution uncertainty and lower upside with greater implementation reliability.
    </interpretation>
  </tradeoff>

  <decision outcome="selected" selected_option="proposal_b">
    <rationale>
      Under a one-award budget, the panel gives decisive weight to delivery confidence, milestone clarity, and team experience. Proposal A remains highly meritorious and technically exciting, but Proposal B offers the stronger likelihood of producing usable results within the funded period.
    </rationale>
    <confidence>moderate</confidence>
  </decision>
</thoughtml>
